en-US.flowIntro: Give each independent task its own branch and working directory. Develop in parallel, then integrate validated changes into main.
en-US.flowCaption: One main line, three independent worktrees. B merges first in this example.
en-US.flowRefresh: Update against current main; resolve conflicts and revalidate
en-US.flowFinish: Merged main → confirm work is saved → remove only the task’s worktree and branches → fast-forward a clean primary checkout.
en-US.flowTiming: This is a process diagram, not a timing estimate. PRs may become ready in any order; each merge must satisfy repository rules against the current integration state.
en-US.flowBoundaries: What worktrees isolate, and what still needs coordination
en-US.flowBoundaryCode: Working files, HEAD and index are separate. Repository history, refs and much Git configuration remain shared; use a different branch for each task. Concurrent edits can still cause merge conflicts. Isolate independent tasks, not individual agents; collaborators on one task agree on file ownership and coordinate Git operations.
en-US.flowBoundaryData: Worktrees do not isolate runtime resources. Assign distinct service ports and task-specific writable test databases. Keep shared authoritative inputs under the owning repository’s DATA_ROOT; generate outputs in distinct task subdirectories. Coordinate shared writes and updates to current/latest pointers.
en-US.flowBoundaryDependencies: Parallelize independent tasks. Agree on interfaces first; for changes across repositories, merge the provider before consumers. Before each merge, validate against current main including earlier merged PRs; if main advances, update or validate the prospective merge and rerun affected checks.
en-US.flowBoundaryReview: Short task branches, required checks and protected main fit common development practice. Worktrees are an optional isolation tool. Automatic merging without separate human review is this workspace’s policy; teams should retain reviews appropriate to risk and repository rules.

en-US.flowGraph: Three branches leave main, work in parallel, pass checks and merge back in order B, A, C.
en-US.flowStep0: Start from the same main commit. Each task uses a different branch and worktree.
en-US.flowStep1: Create branches A, B and C with separate working directories and indexes.
en-US.flowStep2: A, B and C develop in parallel. Their working files are independent.
en-US.flowStep3: Build and test each task, commit the changes and open a PR.
en-US.flowStep4: B passes the required checks and merges first. Main now includes B.
en-US.flowStep5: A updates against the new main, resolves any conflicts and revalidates before merging.
en-US.flowStep6: A passes the required checks and merges into the updated main.
en-US.flowStep7: C also updates and passes checks before merging. All three changes are on main; saved task worktrees and branches can be cleaned up.
en-US.chapterRoots: Keep instructions scoped and resolve machine-local workspace roots.
en-US.chapterI18n: Localize visible UI while keeping data and protocols stable.
en-US.chapterContent: Lead with conclusions and retain inspectable evidence.
en-US.chapterWorkflow: Isolate tasks, validate changes and merge through PRs.
en-US.chapterSafety: Preserve existing work and respect repository controls.
en-US.chapterConfig: Keep settings and credentials outside source repositories.
en-US.chapterData: Use the owning repository’s DATA_ROOT and permanent data paths.

en-US.downloadChineseDetail: For reading; retains the same rules.
en-US.flowActionDevelopDetail: Use a different branch and worktree for each independent task.
en-US.flowActionValidateDetail: Build, test and commit the changes, then open a PR.
en-US.flowActionMergeDetail: Sync current main, resolve conflicts and revalidate before merging.
en-US.flowActionCleanupDetail: Confirm work is saved; clean up only this task and fast-forward a clean primary checkout.
en-US.flowResourceFilesDetail: Separate per worktree. Collaborators on one task agree on file ownership.
en-US.flowResourceHistoryDetail: History, refs and much configuration remain shared. Use different branches and coordinate Git operations.
en-US.flowResourceRuntimeDetail: Worktrees do not isolate runtime resources. Use distinct ports and task-specific writable databases.
en-US.flowResourceDataDetail: Keep inputs at the owning repository’s permanent DATA_ROOT; separate task outputs and coordinate shared writes and current/latest updates.
en-US.flowResourceIntegrationDetail: Parallelize independent tasks; agree on interfaces first and merge providers before consumers across repositories. Revalidate against current main before each merge.

zh-CN.flowIntro: 每个独立任务使用自己的分支与工作目录，同时开发，再把通过验证的改动合入 main。
zh-CN.flowCaption: 一条 main 主线，三个独立 worktree。本例中 B 先合入。
zh-CN.flowOwnFiles: 独立的工作文件与暂存区
zh-CN.flowRefresh: 同步当前 main，解决冲突并重新验证
zh-CN.flowFinish: 合并后的 main → 确认工作已保存 → 仅清理本任务的 worktree 和分支 → 主检出目录干净时快进同步。
zh-CN.flowTiming: 这是一张流程图，不代表耗时。各 PR 可以按不同顺序就绪，每次合并都必须针对当前集成状态满足仓库规则。
zh-CN.flowBoundaries: worktree 隔离了什么，哪些资源仍需协调
zh-CN.flowBoundaryCode: 工作文件、HEAD 和暂存区相互独立，仓库历史、分支引用和许多 Git 配置仍然共享。每个任务使用不同分支，同时修改代码仍可能产生合并冲突。 以独立任务为隔离单位，同一任务的协作者约定文件归属并协调 Git 操作。
zh-CN.flowBoundaryData: worktree 无法隔离运行资源。服务使用不同端口，可写测试数据库按任务隔离。共享权威输入仍放在所属仓库的 DATA_ROOT 下，生成结果使用不同的任务子目录，共享写入需要协调，current/latest 指针的更新也需要协调。
zh-CN.flowBoundaryDependencies: 独立任务适合并行。有依赖的改动先约定接口，跨仓库变更先合并提供方，再合并使用方。 每次合并前针对当前 main 及此前已合入的 PR 验证，主线变化后更新任务分支或验证预期合并结果，并重新运行受影响的检查。
zh-CN.flowBoundaryReview: 短期任务分支、所需检查和受保护的 main 符合常见开发实践，worktree 是可选的隔离工具。无需额外人工审查即可自动合并是本工作区的策略，团队应按风险与仓库规则保留合适的审查。

zh-CN.flowStep0: 从同一个 main 提交出发，每个任务使用不同的分支和 worktree。

zh-CN.flowStep2: A、B、C 同时开发，各自的工作文件相互独立。
